output.review_comment:
The general nearest-rank fix is correct. It uses 1-based rank ceil(p/100*n), p=0 returns the minimum, and it validates that p is in [0, 100]. That legitimately fixes the p30, p40, p90 and p>100 tests.

The blocker is the added special case `if n % 2 == 0 and p == 50:`, which linearly interpolates. It exists only to make test_median_response_time pass: [120, 80, 200, 150] at p50 gives 135. The docstring, which the teammate named as the source of truth, says the result "is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." The README says the same. By the documented method, the answer for that input is ceil(0.5*4) = rank 2, which is 120. The test is wrong, not the code.

This also matters in production. latency_summary calls percentile(..., 50), so the dashboard's p50 would report averaged values whenever the sample count is even. p50 would also use a different method from every other percentile and switch methods depending on whether the sample count is odd or even. The PR has no description, so this deviation isn't disclosed.

Please remove the special-case branch and keep plain nearest-rank. Tell the teammate that test_median_response_time contradicts the docstring and should expect 120. That test change is theirs to approve.
